report.summary: Chunk 12 of correctness.py: implements seeding corpus from real history with _changed_files, _blob, _test_functions, derive_task_from_commit.

handoff.purpose: Implement functions for seeding a corpus from real commit history, including diff parsing, blob retrieval, test function extraction, and task derivation from a commit.

symbols.name: _changed_files
symbols.note: Returns list of (status, relative_path) from git diff --name-status -r --no-renames between a commit and its parent.

symbols.name: _blob
symbols.note: Returns file content at a given revision for a relative path, or None if git show fails.

symbols.name: _test_functions
symbols.note: Extracts pytest node-id -> source mapping from a Python test file using ast; returns dict keyed by function name or ClassName::method_name.

symbols.name: derive_task_from_commit
symbols.note: Proposes a candidate correctness task from a real fix commit; returns dict or None. Uses _changed_files, _blob, _test_functions.

claims.text: The key is the node id form pytest actually accepts -- ``test_x`` for a module-level function, ``ClassName::test_x`` for a method
claims.why: The function builds exactly that: module-level functions keyed by name, class methods keyed as ClassName::method_name.

claims.text: the class qualifier is not optional and getting it wrong makes the node id ``missing``. That is not a hypothetical: the first run of this seeder used unqualified names from ``structcore.extract_units`` (which reports a method as a bare ``test_alive_then_stale``) and the before-state check refuted 19 of 22 candidate nodes in one commit for exactly that reason. The refusal worked; the deriver was still wrong, so it was fixed.
claims.why: The docstring references a historical event and external function 'structcore.extract_units' not present in this chunk; the claim about correctness of the current approach is not verifiable from code alone.

claims.text: ``ast`` rather than a regex or the structural extractor: it is stdlib, it is exact about nesting, and pytest node ids are a Python-only concept anyway. A file that does not parse contributes nothing (the caller then mints nothing from it) rather than contributing guesses.
claims.why: The function uses ast.parse, returns {} on SyntaxError, and only processes .py files.

claims.text: The commit's own diff is the oracle, exactly as in ``mint.py``: what the commit ADDED or CHANGED in a test file is a FAIL_TO_PASS candidate, what it left untouched in the same file is a PASS_TO_PASS candidate, and the base is the commit's parent.
claims.why: The claim references 'mint.py' which is not in this chunk; the logic for f2p/p2p is partially visible (lists are initialized) but the full assignment is not completed in this chunk.

claims.text: NOTHING here is trusted. Every derived node id is a CLAIM that :func:`verify_before_state` then tries to refute by running it on the base; a node id this function gets wrong (a test nested in a class, say, whose real node id carries the class) comes back ``missing`` and takes the task down with it. That is the intended direction: the deriver may be sloppy, the admission gate may not.
claims.why: References verify_before_state which is not in this chunk; the claim about the design is not testable from this code alone.

claims.text: Returns ``None`` when the commit changed no test file -- a real and common case (``efd0ed6`` in this repo's own history is a fix with no test at all), reported by returning nothing rather than by inventing a label.
claims.why: The claim about specific commit efd0ed6 is not verifiable; the function returns None when resolve_revision fails or when no test files are changed (partially visible, but full logic not in chunk).

observations.what: Function _changed_files returns list of tuples; the status character is first element (e.g., 'M', 'A'), but the docstring does not specify the format. The status is checked with startswith('D') in derive_task_from_commit.

Function _test_functions uses ast.get_source_segment to get source text; if that returns None, it falls back to ast.dump(node). This may produce a string representation that is not valid Python, but it is only used as a key? Actually the function returns source segments, not keys; the keys are derived from node names.

derive_task_from_commit initializes overlay, f2p, p2p lists but does not populate them in this chunk; the loop over _changed_files only filters test files and retrieves before/after content and test functions, but does not assign to f2p/p2p. The final return is not shown.
